sentences.zh: 我叫乔纳森·马勒。

sentences.en: I'm a staff writer for The New York Times magazine, and though I haven't used it in a few years, I have a license to walk the tracks of the New York City subway system.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报杂志》的特约撰稿人，虽然我已经有好几年没用了，但我有一张许可证，可以走纽约地铁系统的铁轨。

sentences.en: I've even got a laminated card that I carry in my wallet that says
sentences.zh: 我甚至有一张压膜卡片随身揣在钱包里，上面写着

sentences.en: I'm allowed to go in the hole, as the subway's tunnels are known.
sentences.zh: 我被允许进入“洞穴”，这也是地铁隧道的俗称。

sentences.en: To get that license, I had to take a day-long course that ended with the class actually walking the tracks.
sentences.zh: 为了拿到这张许可证，我不得不参加了一个为期一天的课程，课程结束时全班甚至真的去走了一趟铁轨。

sentences.en: And as part of walking the tracks, you have to prepare for the arrival of a train.
sentences.zh: 作为走铁轨训练的一部分，你必须为火车的到来做好准备。

sentences.en: You do that by tucking your body into a tiny little hole in the wall called a clear-up spot.
sentences.zh: 方法是将身体缩进墙壁上一个称为“避车点”的小洞里。

sentences.en: You wait for the train to come.
sentences.zh: 你等待火车驶来。

sentences.en: You see the light.
sentences.zh: 你看到灯光。

sentences.en: You feel it.
sentences.zh: 你感受到它的存在。

sentences.en: You hear it.
sentences.zh: 你听到它的声音。

sentences.en: And it flies by your face.
sentences.zh: 它从你的脸旁呼啸而过。

sentences.en: And as it comes by, you're just thinking, don't move.
sentences.zh: 当它驶过时，你脑子里只有一个念头：别动。

sentences.en: Don't move.
sentences.zh: 别动。

sentences.en: Don't even scratch your nose.
sentences.zh: 连挠挠鼻子都不要。

sentences.en: I got my license to walk the tracks in
sentences.zh: 我是在

sentences.en: 2017 when I was researching a story on the New York City subway system, how it works, how it doesn't work, and what it would take to fix it.
sentences.zh: 2017年获得走铁轨许可证的，当时我正在调研一篇关于纽约地铁系统的报道：它如何运作，哪里出了问题，以及修复它需要什么。

sentences.en: When I wrote this story, I was basically sounding an alarm when the subway's in desperate shape, the city's in desperate shape, and the subway badly needed help,
sentences.zh: 当我写这篇报道时，我基本上是在拉响警报：当时地铁状况极度糟糕，城市状况极度糟糕，地铁急需帮助，

sentences.en: and it badly needed money.
sentences.zh: 急需资金。

sentences.en: That hasn't changed.
sentences.zh: 这种情况并没有改变。

sentences.en: If anything, the subway is in much worse shape now.
sentences.zh: 如果说有什么不同的话，那就是现在地铁的状况比以前糟得多。

sentences.en: Now, ridership plummeted during the pandemic, of course, and without those fares, the subway system makes even less money.
sentences.zh: 当然，大流行期间客流量骤降，没有了这些车票收入，地铁系统的资金更加捉襟见肘。

sentences.en: When I think about New York City starting to reopen, and I hope it happens soon, I think about all the places people are going to want to go again, to museums, to concerts,
sentences.zh: 每当我想象纽约市开始重新开放——我希望这一天快点到来——我就会想到人们将再次想要前往的所有地方：博物馆、音乐会、

sentences.en: to Broadway, to Yankee Stadium, and they're going to need the subway to do it.
sentences.zh: 百老汇、洋基体育场，而他们需要地铁来实现这一切。

sentences.en: The subway is almost this physical piece of democracy in action.
sentences.zh: 地铁几乎可以说是民主实践的实体体现。

sentences.en: It takes you anywhere you want to go.
sentences.zh: 它带你去任何你想去的地方。

sentences.en: Anyone can ride it at any hour.
sentences.zh: 任何人随时都可以乘坐。

sentences.en: It's truly a marvel.
sentences.zh: 它实在是一个奇迹。

sentences.en: But that's only if it isn't so badly neglected that it's falling apart and can't take you anywhere.
sentences.zh: 但前提是它没有被忽视到破败不堪、无法带你去任何地方的程度。

sentences.en: So here's my story from 2018, The Case for the Subway, read by Robert
sentences.zh: 这是我2018年的报道《地铁的理由》，由罗伯特·

sentences.en: Fass.
sentences.zh: 法斯朗读。

sentences.zh: 这段音频由 Autumn 录制。

sentences.zh: Autumn 是一个您可以下载的应用程序，用于收听来自《纽约时报》、《纽约客》、《名利场》和《大西洋月刊》等出版机构的大量音频故事。

sentences.en: Long before it became an archaic, filthy, profligate symbol of everything wrong with our broken cities,
sentences.zh: 早在它成为我们破败城市中一切弊病的陈旧、肮脏、挥霍的象征之前，

sentences.en: New York's subway was a marvel.
sentences.zh: 纽约地铁曾是一个奇迹。

sentences.en: A mad feat of engineering and an audacious gamble on a preposterously ambitious vision.
sentences.zh: 这是一项疯狂的工程壮举，也是对一个荒谬宏大愿景的大胆豪赌。

sentences.en: The effect it is to have on the city of New York is something larger than any mind can realize, said William Gaynor, the New York mayor who set in motion the primary
sentences.zh: “它对纽约市产生的影响，远超任何人的想象，”启动地铁建设初期的纽约市长威廉·盖诺曾这样说道。

sentences.en: phase of its construction.
sentences.zh: 阶段建设。

sentences.en: A public works project of this scale had never before been undertaken in the
sentences.zh: 美国从未承担过如此规模的公共工程项目。

sentences.en: United States.
sentences.zh: 美国。

sentences.en: And even now, more than a century later, it is hard to fully appreciate what it did for the city, and really, the nation.
sentences.zh: 即使在今天，一个多世纪过去了，我们依然很难充分体会它为这座城市、乃至整个国家所做的一切。

sentences.en: Before the subway, it was by no means a foregone conclusion that
sentences.zh: 在地铁出现之前，纽约能否成为世界上最伟大的城市绝非板上钉钉的事。

sentences.en: New York would become the greatest city on earth.
sentences.zh: 纽约成为地球上最伟大的城市。

sentences.en: Hundreds of thousands of immigrants fleeing poverty and persecution were arriving on its doorstep every year.
sentences.zh: 成千上万为逃离贫困和迫害而来的移民每年涌上它的门槛。

sentences.en: But most of them were effectively marooned, herded into dark, squalid tenements in disease-ridden sluMs. The five boroughs had recently been joined as one city.
sentences.zh: 但他们大多实际上被困住了，被赶进疾病肆虐的贫民窟里黑暗、肮脏的十层公寓。这五个行政区最近才合并为一个城市。

sentences.en: But the farms and villages of Brooklyn, the Bronx, and Queens might as well have been on the other side of the planet from Manhattan's teeming streets.
sentences.zh: 但布鲁克林、布朗克斯和皇后区的农田和村庄，和曼哈顿熙熙攘攘的街道相比，简直就像在地球的另一端。

sentences.en: Bound up in the fate of the city were even larger questions.
sentences.zh: 与这座城市的命运交织在一起的，是更为宏大的问题。

sentences.en: Would America be able to manage the transition from the individualism and insularity
sentences.zh: 美国能否成功实现转型：从定义其19世纪边疆的个人主义与封闭性，

sentences.en: that defined its 19th century frontiers to the creative collaboration and competition of its fast-growing urban centers?
sentences.zh: 转向其快速发展的城市中心的创造性合作与竞争？

sentences.en: Could it adapt and excel in this rapidly changing world?
sentences.zh: 它能否在这个瞬息万变的世界中适应并脱颖而出？

sentences.en: Were cities the past or the future of civilization?
sentences.zh: 城市是文明的过去还是未来？

sentences.en: And then came the subway.
sentences.zh: 随后，地铁诞生了。

sentences.en: Hundreds of miles of tracks shooting out in every direction, carrying millions of immigrants out of the ghettos and into newly built homes, tying together
sentences.zh: 数百英里的铁轨向四面八方延伸，将数百万移民从贫民窟带入新建的住宅中，将

sentences.en: the modern city and enabling it to become a place where anything was possible.
sentences.zh: 现代城市紧密连为一体，使其成为一个一切皆有可能的地方。

sentences.en: It was the arrival of the subway that transformed a seedy neighborhood called Long Acre Square into Times Square, that helped turn a
sentences.zh: 正是地铁的到来，将一个被称为“长英亩广场”的藏污纳垢之地变成了时代广场，将华尔街车站周围短短一平方英里的土地变成了

sentences.en: single square mile surrounding the Wall Street station into the center of global finance, that made Coney
sentences.zh: 全球金融中心，让科尼

sentences.en: Island an amusement park for the masses.
sentences.zh: 岛成为了大众的游乐场。

sentences.en: It was the subway that fueled the astonishing economic growth that built the city's iconic skyscrapers.
sentences.zh: 正是地铁推动了惊人的经济增长，建成了这座城市的标志性摩天大楼。

sentences.en: Other cities had subways, but none threaded through nearly as many neighborhoods as
sentences.zh: 其他城市也有地铁，但没有哪一个像纽约地铁那样贯穿了如此多的街区，

sentences.en: New York's, enabling it to move large numbers of workers between Manhattan and the middle-class boroughs, a cycle that
sentences.zh: 使它能够在大曼哈顿和中产阶级行政区之间运送大量工人，这种循环

sentences.en: repeated itself every day, generating ever more wealth and drawing in ever more people.
sentences.zh: 每天都在重复，创造了更多的财富，吸引了更多的人。

sentences.en: As New York evolved over the decades, the subway was the one constant.
sentences.zh: 随着纽约几十年来的演变，地铁是唯一的恒量。

sentences.en: The very thing that made it possible to repurpose 19th-century factories and warehouses as offices or condominiums, or to reimagine a two-mile spit of land between Manhattan and
sentences.zh: 正是它使得将19世纪的工厂和仓库重新改造为办公室或公寓成为可能，或者将曼哈顿和

sentences.en: Queens that once housed a smallpox hospital as a high-tech university hub.
sentences.zh: 皇后区之间曾设有天花病毒医院的两英里狭长土地重新构想为高科技大学枢纽。

sentences.en: When the city is in crisis, financial or emotional, the subway is always a crucial part of the solution.
sentences.zh: 当城市陷入危机——无论是财务还是情感上的危机——地铁总是解决方案中至关重要的一部分。

sentences.en: The subway led the city recovery from the fiscal calamity of the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 地铁引领这座城市走出了20世纪70年代的财政灾难。

sentences.en: The subway was at the center of the rebuilding of
sentences.zh: 地铁是911袭击后

sentences.en: Lower Manhattan after the September 11th attacks.
sentences.zh: 下曼哈顿重建工作的核心。

sentences.en: The subway got New York back to work after the most devastating storm in the city's history just five years ago.
sentences.zh: 就在五年前，纽约遭遇了城市历史上最具破坏性的风暴后，是地铁让纽约重新恢复了工作。

sentences.en: The questions we are facing today are not so different from the ones our predecessors faced 100 years ago.
sentences.zh: 我们今天面临的问题与我们的前辈在100年前面临的问题并没有太大不同。

sentences.en: Can the gap between rich and poor be closed, or is it destined to continue to widen?
sentences.zh: 富人和穷人之间的差距能够缩小，还是注定会继续拉大？

sentences.en: Can we put the future needs of a city and a nation above the narrow present-day interests of a few?
sentences.zh: 我们能否将城市和国家未来的需求置于少数人狭隘的当今利益之上？

sentences.en: Can we use a portion of the monumental sums of wealth that we are generating to invest in an inclusive and competitive future?
sentences.zh: 我们能否利用我们正在创造的巨额财富中的一部分，来投资于一个包容且具有竞争力的未来？

sentences.en: The answer to all of these questions is still rumbling beneath New York City.
sentences.zh: 所有这些问题的答案依然在纽约市的地下轰鸣作响。

sentences.en: For all the changes in transportation technology since the first tunnels were dug, the rise of the automobile, the proliferation of bike lanes and ferries,
sentences.zh: 尽管自从第一条隧道开挖以来交通技术发生了种种变化——汽车的兴起、自行车道和轮渡的激增、

sentences.en: our growing addiction to ride-hailing apps, and dreams of a future filled with autonomous vehicles, the subway remains the only way to move large numbers of people around the city.
sentences.zh: 我们对网约车应用日益增长的依赖，以及对充满自动驾驶汽车的未来的梦想——地铁仍然是将大量人员运送过城市的唯一途径。

sentences.en: Today, New York's subway carries close to six million people every day, more than twice the entire population of Chicago.
sentences.zh: 如今，纽约地铁每天运送近六00万人，是芝加哥总人口的两倍多。

sentences.en: The subway may no longer be a technological marvel, but it continues to perform a daily magic trick.
sentences.zh: 地铁或许不再是一个技术奇迹，但它仍在上演着日常的魔术。

sentences.en: It brings people together, but it also spreads people out.
sentences.zh: 它将人们聚集在一起，但也把人们分散开来。

sentences.en: It is this paradox, these constant expansions and contractions, like a beating heart, that keep the human capital flowing and the city growing.
sentences.zh: 正是这种悖论，这种不断地扩张与收缩，就像跳动的心脏一样，保持着人力资本的流动和城市的生长。

sentences.en: New York's subway has no zones and no hours of operation.
sentences.zh: 纽约地铁没有区票划分，也没有运营时间的限制。

sentences.en: It connects rich and poor neighborhoods alike.
sentences.zh: 它同样连接着富裕和贫穷的社区。

sentences.en: The subway has never been segregated.
sentences.zh: 地铁从来没有实行过种族隔离。

sentences.en: It is always open, and the fare is always the same, no matter how far you need to go.
sentences.zh: 它始终开放，无论你需要走多远，票价始终如一。

sentences.en: In New York, movement, anywhere, anytime, is a right.
sentences.zh: 在纽约，随时随地出行是一种权利。

sentences.en: Most countries treat subway systems as national assets.
sentences.zh: 大多数国家将地铁系统视为国家资产。

sentences.en: They understand that their cities are their great wealth creators and equality enablers, and that cities don't work without subways.
sentences.zh: 他们明白，城市是他们巨大的财富创造者和机会平等促成者，没有地铁，城市就无法运转。

sentences.en: The public-private corporation that runs Hong Kong's subway expects 99.9% of its trains to run on time, and they do.
sentences.zh: 运营香港地铁的公私合营公司期望其99.9%的列车准点运行，而他们确实做到了。

sentences.en: If you are traveling to the airport, you can also check your luggage at a central downtown train station and not see it again until you've landed at your destination.
sentences.zh: 如果你要去机场，还可以在市中心的中央火车站托运行李，直到抵达目的地落地后才能再次看到它。

sentences.en: Imagine.
sentences.zh: 想象一下。

sentences.en: China has been feverishly building new metro systems in cities across the country, a recognition that
sentences.zh: 中国一直在狂热地在全国各地的城市建造新的地铁系统，这是一种认识：

sentences.en: subways are the only way to keep pace with the nation's rapid urbanization and the needs of its citizens.
sentences.zh: 地铁是跟上国家快速城市化步伐和满足公民需求的唯一途径。

sentences.en: And it's not just new cities that are seeing major investments in their subways.
sentences.zh: 不仅是新城市在其地铁上看到重大投资。

sentences.en: Two decades ago, the decline of London's underground became a national crisis.
sentences.zh: 二十年前，伦敦地铁的衰落成了一场国家危机。

sentences.en: Now it's moving toward running driverless trains.
sentences.zh: 现在它正朝着运行无人驾驶列车迈进。

sentences.en: For that matter, Los Angeles, Los Angeles, recently embarked on a 40-year, $120 billion project to build out its mass transit system.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，洛杉矶最近也启动了一项为期40年、耗资1200亿美元的项目，以建设其公共交通系统。

sentences.en: New York City's subway, meanwhile, is falling apart.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，纽约市的地铁却在崩溃。

sentences.en: If you are a regular rider, you know this firsthand.
sentences.zh: 如果你是常客，你对此有着切身体会。

sentences.en: But even if you aren't, it has probably become difficult to ignore all the stories about the system's failure.
sentences.zh: 但即使你不是，大概也很难忽视所有关于该系统故障的报道。

sentences.en: The F train that was trapped between stations for close to an hour without power or air conditioning.
sentences.zh: F线列车在两站之间被困近一个小时，没有电力或空调。

sentences.en: The Q train that derailed in
sentences.zh: 在

sentences.en: Brooklyn.
sentences.zh: 布鲁克林脱轨的Q线列车。

sentences.en: The track fire on the A-Line in Harlem that sent nine passengers to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 哈莱姆区A线列车的轨道火灾导致九名乘客被送往医院。

sentences.en: The cumulative impression of all these miserable underground experiences, and all these stories
sentences.zh: 所有这些悲惨的地下经历，以及所有关于这些悲惨地下经历的报道，

sentences.en: about miserable underground experiences, is that the situation is hopeless, that the subway cannot be fixed.
sentences.zh: 给人留下的总印象是情况无可救药，地铁已经修不好了。

sentences.en: The subway has been wrecked, and in this era of short-term thinking and government mistrust,
sentences.zh: 地铁已经被毁了，在这个短期思维和政府不信任的时代，

sentences.en: public works projects with benefits larger than any single mind can realize are no longer possible.
sentences.zh: 那些带来超乎任何单一个人想象的巨大利益的公共工程项目已不再可能实现。

sentences.en: But it is possible to fix the subway, and we muSt. Our failure to do so would be a collective and historic act of self-destruction.
sentences.zh: 但是修复地铁是可能的，我们也必须这样做。如果我们做不到，将是集体和历史性的自我毁灭行为。

sentences.en: One, who wrecked the subway?
sentences.zh: 第一，是谁毁了地铁？

sentences.en: The Metropolitan Transportation Authority, the government agency that operates the subway,
sentences.zh: 大都会交通管理局（MTA），即运营地铁的政府机构，

sentences.en: uses the catch-all word incident to describe all the various events that impede the system's healthy functioning.
sentences.zh: 使用“事件”这个包罗万象的词来描述阻碍系统健康运转的各种事件。

sentences.en: Every one of these incidents triggers an investigation resulting in an incident report, a minute-by-minute account of what went wrong and the steps taken to resolve the issue.
sentences.zh: 每一个此类事件都会引发调查，从而产生一份事件报告，详细记录了哪里出了问题以及为解决问题所采取的步骤，精确到每分每秒。

sentences.en: Thousands of these reports are produced every month.
sentences.zh: 每个月都会产生数千份这样的报告。

sentences.en: A random sampling of incidents from a single recent day include signal trouble, switch trouble, unruly persons, track circuit failure,
sentences.zh: 最近某一天中随机抽样的事件包括：信号故障、道岔故障、无理取闹人员、轨道电路故障、

sentences.en: delayed by track-slash-work gangs, water condition, fire-slash-smoke conditions, debris on road bed, brakes fail to charge, and sparks issuing.
sentences.zh: 轨道/施工作业队延误、水情、火灾/烟雾情况、路基杂物、刹车无法充气以及冒火花。

sentences.en: Among the most common were excess dwell time and insufficient capacity-slash-crowding.
sentences.zh: 其中最常见的是列车停留时间过长和运力不足/拥挤。

sentences.en: Translation, too many passengers, not enough trains.
sentences.zh: 翻译过来就是：乘客太多，列车不够。

sentences.en: All these problems lead to one really big problem.
sentences.zh: 所有这些问题都导致了一个真正的大问题。

sentences.en: The trains are terminally late, obstructed daily by a cascade of system failures.
sentences.zh: 列车无限期晚点，每天都受到一连串系统故障的阻碍。

sentences.en: During the first three months of 2017, three-quarters of the subway's lines were chronically behind schedule.
sentences.zh: 在2017年的前三个月里，四分之三的地铁线路长期落后于时间表。

sentences.en: The worst offender, the two-train, was late nearly 70% of the time.
sentences.zh: 情况最糟糕的是2号线，近70%的时间都在晚点。

sentences.en: For a delayed rider wondering whom to blame, it's tempting to begin with the people you can see,
sentences.zh: 对于想知道该怪谁的晚点乘客来说，很容易从你能看到的人开始找起，

sentences.en: the 7,000 or so men and women, track cleaners, inspectors, flaggers, and other orange-vested
sentences.zh: 大约7000名男性和女性，包括轨道清洁工、检查员、旗手和其他身穿橙色背心的

sentences.en: MTA employees, charged with preventing these incidents and keeping the trains moving.
sentences.zh: MTA员工，他们负责预防这些事件并保持列车运行。

sentences.en: On a steamy morning in August, I sat among a small group of them in a dingy, defunct public elementary school in
sentences.zh: 在一个闷热的八月早晨，我坐在布鲁克林格雷夫森德一所昏暗、废弃的公立小学里的一小群人中间，

sentences.en: Gravesend, Brooklyn, that serves as the MTA's transit learning center.
sentences.zh: 这里现在是MTA的交通学习中心。

sentences.en: Taped to the classroom wall were yellowing tabloid clips of a different kind of subway horror story.
sentences.zh: 教室墙上贴着用黄色胶带固定着的、有关另一种地铁恐怖故事的小报剪报。

sentences.en: Man under, rail horror, hit third track and lived.
sentences.zh: “卧轨者，铁轨惊魂，撞上第三轨道却生还”。

sentences.en: A tableau that lent the one-day safety course, a requirement for all MTA employees and contractors, some of the flavor of those grisly low-budget driver's ed videos
sentences.zh: 这个场景给这个成为所有MTA员工和承包商必修课的一日安全课程，平添了几分那些骇人听闻的低成本驾驶培训视频的色彩，

sentences.en: designed to scare teenagers straight.
sentences.zh: 这些视频旨在吓唬青少年走正道。

sentences.en: If you should do something silly today, like get hit by a train, you cannot sue New York City Transit, my instructor Jim Fortin said as he distributed release forms to the class.
sentences.zh: “如果你今天做出一些愚蠢的事情，比如被火车撞了，你不能起诉纽约市交通局，”我的教练吉姆·福廷在向全班分发免责声明时说道。

sentences.en: It's a common occurrence.
sentences.zh: 这是常有的事。

sentences.en: A passenger is killed on the tracks pretty much every week.
sentences.zh: 差不多每星期都有乘客在铁轨上丧生。

sentences.en: The course would end with a walk on a live track.
sentences.zh: 课程将以在带电铁轨上行走结束。

sentences.en: If I survived the day, I would receive a laminated license qualifying me to work in the tunnels of the New York City subway system, in the hole as it is known.
sentences.zh: 如果我能在这天活下来，我将获得一张压膜许可证，证明我有资格在纽约市地铁系统的隧道里工作，也就是所谓的“洞穴”中工作。

sentences.en: Fortin walked us through the potential hazards that awaited us.
sentences.zh: 福廷向我们详细介绍了等待着我们的潜在危险。

sentences.en: He taught us the proper arm motions to use if we ever found ourselves needing to signal to an oncoming train to stop.
sentences.zh: 他教导我们正确的胳膊动作，以防我们需要向迎面驶来的火车发出停车信号。

sentences.en: After a short multiple-choice test and a break for lunch, we were issued orange vests, flashlights, helmets, and safety goggles.
sentences.zh: 经过简短的选择题测试和午餐休息后，我们领到了橙色背心、手电筒、头盔和安全护目镜。

sentences.en: Our group walked to a nearby N station, rode a few stops, transferred to the R, and got off at 53rd Street, where we walked to the end of the platform
sentences.zh: 我们一行人步行到附近的N线车站，坐了几站，换乘R线，在53街下车，然后步行到站台尽头

sentences.en: and climbed down a ladder onto the tracks.
sentences.zh: 然后顺着梯子爬到轨道上。

sentences.en: Fortin soon directed us to what he called clear-up spots, small, shallow openings built into the walls of the narrow tunnels that we had been taught that morning to identify.
sentences.zh: 福廷很快带我们来到他所谓的清理点，这是狭窄隧道墙壁上修建的小而浅的开口，我们那天早上刚学过如何识别它们。

sentences.en: A train was coming.
sentences.zh: 一辆列车正驶来。

sentences.en: I stuffed my flashlight into my back pocket and tucked myself into the tiny space, remembering Fortin's instructions, get in, get centered, don't move.
sentences.zh: 我把手电筒塞进后裤兜，按照福廷的指示把自己缩进那个狭小的空间：进去，居中，别动。

sentences.en: I could hear the train approaching and see its headlight out of the corner of my eye.
sentences.zh: 我能听到列车驶近的声音，眼角余光也瞥见它的前灯。

sentences.en: In about 30 seconds, a string of 45-ton steel cars was thundering by, just 18 inches from my frozen body.
sentences.zh: 大约30秒内，一连串重达45吨的钢制车厢轰隆隆地驶过，距离我僵硬的身体只有18英寸。

sentences.en: It was terrifying, but also thrilling, like the entire Industrial Revolution was speeding past my face.
sentences.zh: 这太吓人了，但也极为刺激，就像整场工业革命正从我的眼前呼啸而过。

sentences.en: At point-blank range, subway cars seem invincible.
sentences.zh: 近距离看，地铁列车似乎坚不可摧。

sentences.en: In fact, they can be laid low by something as insignificant as a broken bolt or a can of soda, which, when resting against the third rail,
sentences.zh: 事实上，像一颗断裂的螺栓或一个苏打水罐这样微不足道的东西，只要靠在第三轨上，就能将其击垮，

sentences.en: might heat up and ignite a scrap of newspaper, causing a track fire, the source of hundreds of delays every month.
sentences.zh: 它可能会发热并点燃一张废报纸，引发轨道火灾，这也是每月数百起延误的根源。

sentences.en: Every inch of the system's rails is supposed to be checked twice a week for imperfections.
sentences.zh: 该系统轨道的每一英寸理应每周检查两次，以查找瑕疵。

sentences.en: Much of this work happens overnight, when the frequency of trains on this 24-hour system decreases and workers are able to move more freely on the tracks.
sentences.zh: 这项工作大部分在夜间进行，此时这个24小时运行系统的列车班次减少，工人们能够在轨道上更自由地活动。

sentences.en: While the rest of the city is sleeping, there's a whole industrial ballet going on underground that most people have no idea about.
sentences.zh: 当城市其余部分在沉睡时，地下正在进行一场大多数人一无所知的宏大工业芭蕾。

sentences.en: John Samuelson, a track inspector who now runs the Transport Workers Union of America, told me, it's like friggin' Brigadoon down there.
sentences.zh: 轨道检查员、现任美国交通工人工会负责人约翰·萨缪尔森告诉我：“地下这地方简直就像虚构的世外桃源布里加顿。”

sentences.en: And yet a recent study found that only 3% of the tracks in stations meet the MTA's own standards for cleanliness.
sentences.zh: 然而最近的一项研究发现，车站中只有3%的轨道符合大都会运输署（MTA）自己的清洁标准。

sentences.en: Workers face an even more insidious challenge than trash in the form of water.
sentences.zh: 工人们面临着比垃圾更阴险的挑战——水。

sentences.en: Many parts of the system are below the water table, and its lines course through neighborhoods that were once lush farmland.
sentences.zh: 该系统的许多部分位于地下水位以下，其线路穿过曾经是肥沃农田的街区。

sentences.en: On a dry day, the MTA pumps 13 million gallons of water from the system.
sentences.zh: 在干燥的日子里，MTA要从系统中抽出1300万加仑的水。

sentences.en: Over time, the water corrodes the system, rusting and rotting its infrastructure, and yet sealing and grouting these leaks often requires
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，水会腐蚀系统，使其基础设施生锈腐烂，然而对这些漏水处进行密封和灌浆往往需要

sentences.en: rerouting service on lines, further frustrating riders.
sentences.zh: 改道分流线路，从而进一步让乘客感到沮丧。

sentences.en: Next year, the L train will begin a shutdown that will last at least 15 months for repairs to its East River Tunnel, which flooded during Hurricane Sandy.
sentences.zh: 明年，L线将开始停运，持续至少15个月，以修复在桑迪飓风中被淹的东河隧道。

sentences.en: Some 225,000 people will have to find a new way to get in and out of
sentences.zh: 大约有22.5万人将不得不寻找新的方式来进出

sentences.en: Manhattan every day.
sentences.zh: 曼哈顿。

sentences.en: No matter how diligent they may be, 7,000-odd orange-vested maintenance workers are simply not enough to keep the deteriorating system, with its 665 miles of passenger-carrying
sentences.zh: 无论他们多么勤勉，大约7000名身穿橙色背心的维护工人根本不足以维持这个不断恶化的系统正常运行，其拥有665英里的载客

sentences.en: track, enough to reach all the way to Indianapolis, on schedule.
sentences.zh: 轨道——长得足以一直延伸到印第安纳波利斯——按时运行。

sentences.en: All the real problems must begin elsewhere, further up the chain of command.
sentences.zh: 所有真正的问题一定都始于别处，始于指挥链的更高层。

sentences.en: Pretty much every decision that destroys your commute happens not below ground, but above it.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有毁掉你通勤体验的决定，都不是在地下做出，而是在地上。

sentences.en: In an unmarked building on the west side of Manhattan called the Rail Control Center.
sentences.zh: 在曼哈顿西侧一栋名为铁路控制中心的无标号大楼里。

sentences.en: Here, men and women sit at computer consoles behind large wall-mounted schematic track and station displays in a high-ceilinged, windowless command space, directing the changes,
sentences.zh: 在这里，男男女女坐在高挑无窗、宽敞的指挥大厅里，面对着装有大型壁挂式示意轨道和车站显示屏的电脑控制台，指挥着调度变道，

sentences.en: moving a local train to an express track, taking a train out of service, that determine the daily transportation fate of thousands, sometimes millions of passengers.
sentences.zh: 将列车从慢车道调到快车道，将列车停运，这些决定了成千上万、有时甚至是数百万乘客的日常交通命运。

sentences.en: When I visited the facility several months ago, I was greeted by the official who oversees all these disruptions, Barry Greenblatt.
sentences.zh: 几个月前我参观该设施时，负责处理所有这些混乱状况的官员巴里·格林布拉特接待了我。

sentences.en: A tall, slender man in a gray suit, with two Bic pens in his shirt pocket, and a silver tie clip so tarnished that you barely make out the letters on it, MTA.
sentences.zh: 他是一位身材高瘦、穿着灰色西装的男士，衬衣口袋里插着两支百能笔，银色领带夹已经褪色得几乎看不清上面的字母“MTA”。

sentences.en: Greenblatt is the authority's vice president and chief officer for service delivery, Department of Subways.
sentences.zh: 格林布拉特是该机构负责服务交付的副总裁兼首席官，隶属于地铁部门。

sentences.en: It's his job to run the trains.
sentences.zh: 运营列车是他的工作。

sentences.en: Greenblatt, a 31-year veteran of the MTA, grew up in Forest Hills, Queens, without a car.
sentences.zh: 格林布拉特在MTA工作了31年，是在皇后区森林小丘长大的，家里没有汽车。

sentences.en: I started riding trains and buses by myself pretty much from the time I was five years old, he told me after we settled into a conference room overlooking the command center.
sentences.zh: 当我们坐在俯瞰指挥中心的会议室里定下神来后，他告诉我：“我基本上从五岁起就开始独自坐火车和公交车了。”

sentences.en: He became a bus driver when he graduated from college, fulfilling a childhood dream, and has been an employee of the MTA ever since, gradually moving up the ladder to his current
sentences.zh: 大学毕业后他成为了一名公交车司机，实现了童年的梦想，此后便一直是MTA的员工，一步步晋升到目前的

sentences.en: position.
sentences.zh: 职位。

sentences.en: We operate the trains, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说：“我们运营列车。”

sentences.en: We try to run them on time, 5.66 million average daily riders, 1.7 billion annual riders.
sentences.zh: “我们努力让它们准点运行，日均载客量566万，年载客量1.7亿。”

sentences.en: Right now there are 585 trains out there.
sentences.zh: “现在外面有585列火车。”

sentences.en: We will run 8,477 one-way trips over the course of a day.
sentences.zh: “一天下来我们要运行8477趟单程。”

sentences.en: We hope to have 8,477 on-time trains.
sentences.zh: “我们希望有8477列准点列车。”

sentences.en: We're not going to do it today.
sentences.zh: “我们今天做不到。”

sentences.en: Greenblatt's morning began with a 2.30 a.m.
sentences.zh: 格林布拉特的一天始于凌晨2点30分

sentences.en: phone call.
sentences.zh: 的一通电话。

sentences.en: An operator moving a train out of storage at a yard in East New York, Brooklyn, had driven through a stop signal, damaging the switch beneath him.
sentences.zh: 一名操作员将一列车从布鲁克林东纽约的一个停车场开出来时，闯过了停车信号灯，撞坏了下方的道岔。

sentences.en: The first question we would ask is whether it is going to have any impact on service,
sentences.zh: 格林布拉特说：

sentences.en: Greenblatt said.
sentences.zh: “我们要问的第一个问题是它是否会对服务产生任何影响。”

sentences.en: A few hours later, at 5.10 a.m., he received a text message about another incident.
sentences.zh: 几个小时后，即早上5点10分，他收到了一条关于另一起事故的短信。

sentences.en: A passenger had called from the Park Place station near City Hall to report that there was smoke on the tracks.
sentences.zh: 一名乘客从市政厅附近的公园广场站打来电话，报告轨道上有烟雾。

sentences.en: Seven minutes later, the New York City Police Department reported via an internal communications line known as the Six Wire that a transformer may have exploded in the station.
sentences.zh: 七分钟后，纽约市警察局通过被称为“六号线”的内部通信线路报告称，站内可能有一个变压器爆炸了。

sentences.en: Greenblatt managed the response.
sentences.zh: 格林布拉特负责处理这一突发情况。

sentences.en: Service on the two and three lines was rerouted, and several teams were deployed to Park
sentences.zh: 2号线和3号线的服务被改道，几支队伍被派往公园

sentences.en: Place to figure out what was going on.
sentences.zh: 广场弄清楚发生了什么。

sentences.en: They soon discovered that a chunk of metal about 18 inches long had fallen onto the tracks, breaking through the third rail protection board and shorting out the power.
sentences.zh: 他们很快发现，一块大约18英寸长的金属块落在了轨道上，砸穿了第三轨保护板并导致电源短路。

sentences.en: If you bridge the third rail, which has 600 volts of electricity, to the signal rail, which has
sentences.zh: 格林布拉特说：

sentences.en: 12 volts of electricity, Greenblatt said, it's going to blow things.
sentences.zh: “如果你把拥有600伏电力的第三轨，和拥有12伏电力的信号轨搭接起来，就会把东西炸毁。”

sentences.en: The rail control center's chief officer, Paul McPhee, showed me a picture on his phone of the charred board, which looked as though it
sentences.zh: 铁路控制中心首席官保罗·麦克菲在手机上向我展示了一张烧焦的电路板照片，看起来就像是

sentences.en: could have been pulled from the fire pit at a campsite.
sentences.zh: 从露营地的篝火坑里拉出来的一样。

sentences.en: It took about two and a half hours for the temporary repairs to be completed and full power to be restored.
sentences.zh: 临时抢修花了一个半小时左右才完成，并恢复了全电供应。

sentences.en: The trains could now start running again, but were required to move at reduced speeds in the vicinity of the station.
sentences.zh: 列车现在可以重新开始运行，但被要求在车站附近减速行驶。

sentences.en: We're operating in a degraded mode right now, Greenblatt said.
sentences.zh: 格林布拉特说：“我们目前处于降级运行模式。”

sentences.en: System-wide, the biggest source of subway delays is simple overcrowding.
sentences.zh: 在整个系统中，地铁延误的最大原因就是单纯的过度拥挤。

sentences.en: In the 1990s, after a derailment killed five passengers and a collision killed a train operator, the MTA started actively slowing down its trains.
sentences.zh: 20世纪90年代，在一次脱轨事故导致五名乘客死亡、一次相撞事故导致一名列车员丧生后，MTA开始主动让列车减速。

sentences.en: This has reduced throughput, the number of trains that move through the system at any given time, which has increased crowding.
sentences.zh: 这降低了通行能力，即在任何给定时间内穿过该系统的列车数量，从而加剧了拥挤。

sentences.en: And when the subway becomes more crowded, it grows slower still, with trains stuck in stations while knots of passengers fight their way in and out of cars.
sentences.zh: 而当地铁变得更加拥挤时，它的速度就会变得更慢，列车滞留在车站里，一团团乘客艰难地在车厢里挤进挤出。

sentences.en: As ridership grew from 2012 to 2016, the end-to-end running time during peak hours on the numbered lines increased by more than six minutes.
sentences.zh: 随着2012年至2016年客流量的增长，编号线路在高峰时段的端到端运行时间增加了六分钟以上。

sentences.en: Average train speeds are now slower than they were in 1950.
sentences.zh: 如今的平均列车运行速度比1950年还要慢。

sentences.en: The subway could be both faster and safer if all of it were controlled by a computer-based signal system, which would automatically ensure that trains
sentences.zh: 如果整个系统都由基于计算机的信号系统控制，地铁本可以更快、更安全，该系统将自动确保列车

sentences.en: are always operating at the maximum safe speed, with the narrowest possible distance between them.
sentences.zh: 始终以最大安全速度运行，并且它们之间的距离保持在尽可能小的范围内。

sentences.en: Instead, much of the subway uses a signal system that dates to the 1920s and 30s.
sentences.zh: 相反，地铁的大部分路段使用的是可以追溯到20世纪20和30年代的信号系统。

sentences.en: What that means didn't really hit home for me until I visited the signal repair shop at the 215th Street rail yard in Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 这意味着什么，直到我参观了曼哈顿215街铁路场的信号修理厂，我才真正深有体会。

sentences.en: Technicians were hunched over cast-iron gadgets—stop motors, compressors, track relays—that looked as if they belonged in the workshop of an eccentric antique collector.
sentences.zh: 技术人员正弯腰驼背地摆弄着铸铁小玩意——止动马达、压缩机、轨道继电器——看起来它们似乎应该属于某个古怪古董收藏家的作坊。

sentences.en: In the machine shop downstairs,
sentences.zh: 在楼下的机械车间里，

sentences.en: I saw workers making mounting brackets and ball bearings.
sentences.zh: 我看到工人们在制作安装支架和滚珠轴承。

sentences.en: Most of the system's 472 stations need some kind of major repair or wholesale renovation.
sentences.zh: 该系统的472个车站中，大多数都需要某种程度的大修或全面翻新。

sentences.zh: 需要增设电梯。

sentences.en: Cracked tiles and rusty columns need to be replaced.
sentences.zh: 需要更换开裂的瓷砖和生锈的柱子。

sentences.en: Stairwells and entryways need to be enlarged.
sentences.zh: 需要扩建楼梯间和入口。

sentences.en: Flood-prone openings need to be waterproof.
sentences.zh: 易涝开口需要做好防水。

sentences.en: Ventilation plants need to be rebuilt.
sentences.zh: 需要重建通风设备。

sentences.en: All the platforms need to be sealed off from the tracks with automatic sliding doors to prevent passengers from throwing trash on the rail bed
sentences.zh: 所有站台都需要用自动滑门与轨道隔开，以防止乘客向轨道床扔垃圾

sentences.zh: 并阻止他们跌落、跳下或被推落到列车下。

sentences.zh: 需要重修整个系统隧道中的急转弯，使其没有那么陡峭，从而允许更高的速度，进而容纳更多的列车。

sentences.en: When he left work that night, it had not felt any different from any other day on the job.

sentences.en: I don't know if I like the word meltdown so much, Greenblatt said.
sentences.zh: 格林布拉特说：“我不知道自己有多喜欢‘瘫痪’这个词。”

sentences.en: And on a rainy, windswept night in early September, his press office invited a small group of reporters and local camera crews to assemble

sentences.en: Spotlights hung from rusty columns, a dozen or so chairs were arrayed before a lectern and a video monitor.
sentences.zh: 聚光灯从生锈的柱子上悬挂下来，讲台和视频监视器前摆放着大约十多把椅子。

sentences.zh: 午夜前不久，科莫通过一个大型通风人孔戏剧性地登场，他身穿熨烫平整的休闲裤、流苏靴和印有

sentences.zh: 纽约州徽章的风衣，顺着金属梯子爬了下来，并宣布他将地铁随地乱扔垃圾的罚款提高到

sentences.zh: 100美元，并购买一些全新的巨型吸尘器来清理轨道。

sentences.zh: 这些举措是科莫8.36亿美元纽约市地铁行动计划的一部分，该计划是去年夏天由

sentences.zh: 新上任的MTA主席乔·洛塔公布的，他几年前也曾管理过该机构。

sentences.zh: 谁来承担那8.36亿美元仍然是一个颇具争议的问题。

sentences.zh: 科莫提出承担一半，并称市政府应该承担其余部分。白思豪拒绝了，

sentences.en: noting that the city had already given the MTA, which it did not control, billions of dollars in taxes.
sentences.zh: 指出市政府已经向其并不控制的MTA提供了数十亿美元的税收。

sentences.en: The plan remains only partially funded.
sentences.zh: 该计划目前只得到了部分资金支持。

sentences.zh: 对于地铁来说，这是一个熟悉的困境。

sentences.en: When the MTA first took control of the system in 1968, the idea was to use toll money from bridges
sentences.zh: 当MTA于1968年首次接管该系统时，其想法是利用桥梁

sentences.zh: 和隧道的通行费来补贴地铁，但这一方案只提供了所需资金的一小部分。

sentences.zh: 多年来，州政府和联邦政府一直填补资金缺口。

sentences.en: But beginning in the 1990s,
sentences.zh: 但从20世纪90年代开始，

sentences.zh: 此后，它一直在为新的收入来源苦苦挣扎。

sentences.en: Cuomo, for all his homilies about American greatness being the product of what we built, has also rejected some efforts to add new revenue sources to the subway.
sentences.zh: 科莫尽管发表了许多关于美国伟大是我们的建设成果的陈词滥调，但也拒绝了一些为地铁增加新收入来源的努力。

sentences.en: In 2015, a state assemblyman from Brooklyn, Jim Brennan, wrote a bill that would have steered a small but escalating percentage of state personal income tax to the authority.
sentences.zh: 2015年，来自布鲁克林的州议员吉姆·布伦南写了一项法案，旨在将州个人所得税中一小部分但不断增加的比例引导至该机构。

sentences.en: Cuomo's staff dismissed the idea.
sentences.zh: 科莫的工作人员驳回了这个想法。

sentences.en: They said the MTA wouldn't be able to spend the money.
sentences.zh: 他们称MTA将无法把这笔钱花出去。

sentences.zh: 布伦南告诉我，建筑业已经达到了饱和状态。

sentences.en: Of course, when I would talk to Tom Prendergast, the chairman of the MTA at the time, and his top people, they would go,

sentences.en: Yes, yes, we can spend the money.
sentences.zh: “可以，可以，我们能把钱花出去。”

sentences.en: Give us the money.
sentences.zh: “把钱给我们吧。”

sentences.en: In fact, the MTA has often proved all too capable of spending money, with construction costs well beyond what other cities spend on similar projects.
sentences.zh: 事实上，MTA往往被证明非常善于花钱，其建设成本远远超出了其他城市在同类项目上的花费。

sentences.en: It's fair to blame the whole New York political establishment,
sentences.zh: 指责整个纽约政治建制派是公平的，

sentences.en: Cuomo, de Blasio, and their counterparts stretching back decades or presiding over the subway's decline.
sentences.zh: 科莫、德布拉西奥以及他们几十年来或主持地铁衰落的前辈们。

sentences.en: But the real political problem is, at root, a structural one.
sentences.zh: 但真正的政治问题，从根本上说是一个结构性问题。

sentences.zh: 地铁靠着一拼凑的临时税收勉强维持，这些税收由一位代表着大都市圈以外数百万选民的州长实施和监督。

sentences.zh: 这种分歧在城市内部也有着更为狭隘的表现，代表汽车至上外围行政区社区的议员们继续反对拥堵费计划，

sentences.zh: 现年84岁的拉维奇是那种如今已不多见的公民领袖，他是一位城市理想主义者，其职业生涯一直在公共部门和私营部门之间穿梭。

sentences.en: His grandfather fled the pogroms in Russia, and, classic New York story, created a successful construction business from nothing.
sentences.zh: 他的祖父为逃避俄罗斯的暴动，白手起家创办了一家成功的建筑公司，这是典型的纽约故事。

sentences.en: He lost everything in the Depression, and then his son, Ravitch's father, made his name building apartment buildings on Central Park WeSt.
sentences.zh: 他在大萧条中失去了所有，随后他的儿子、也就是拉维奇的父亲，因在中央公园西路建造公寓楼而声名鹊起。

sentences.en: Ravitch followed his father into the real estate business.
sentences.zh: 拉维奇跟随父亲进入了房地产行业。

sentences.en: In the 1960s, he served on President Lyndon Johnson's
sentences.zh: 20世纪60年代，他曾在林登·约翰逊总统的

sentences.en: National Commission on Urban Problems, and in 1973, after 12 years of trying, he completed Waterside, a $78 million, 1,470-unit development for low- and middle-income families
sentences.zh: 国家城市问题委员会任职；1973年，经过12年的不懈努力，他完成了位于东河边、靠近联合国总部南侧的“滨水区”项目，这是一个耗资7800万美元、拥有1470套住房的开发项目，

sentences.en: on the East River, just south of the United Nations.
sentences.zh: 专为中低收入家庭建造。

sentences.en: A couple of years later,
sentences.zh: 几年后，

sentences.en: Ravitch played a critical role in rescuing New York City from its fiscal crisis, helping to persuade the Teachers Union to invest $150 million of its pension fund
sentences.zh: 拉维奇在拯救纽约市财政危机中发挥了关键作用，他协助说服教师工会将其养老基金中的1.5亿美元

sentences.en: in a new series of city bonds.
sentences.zh: 投资于新发行的城市债券系列。

sentences.en: And in 1979, he was named chairman of the MTA.
sentences.zh: 1979年，他被任命为MTA主席。

sentences.en: Ravitch didn't need the job, or even really want it.
sentences.zh: 拉维奇并不需要这份工作，甚至也不是真的很想干。

sentences.en: He waived his salary and took to wearing a bulletproof vest in public after someone threatening to kill him shot an MTA police officer at his office.
sentences.zh: 他放弃了薪水，并在有人威胁要杀死他并向他办公室的一名MTA警察开枪后，开始在公共场合穿防弹衣。

sentences.en: But he was a child of the New Deal and a passionate believer in the subway, which at the time was in even worse shape than it is today.
sentences.zh: 但他是一个新政时期的孩子，也是地铁的狂热信仰者，当时的地铁状况甚至比现在还要糟糕。

sentences.en: During the fiscal crisis, drastic funding cuts had spun the subway into a downward spiral of deteriorating tracks, malfunctioning cars, increasing crime, and falling ridership,
sentences.zh: 在财政危机期间，急剧的资金削减让地铁陷入了轨道老化、车辆故障、犯罪率上升以及客流量下降的恶性循环，

sentences.en: a steep decline that tracked the city's own post-industrial collapse.
sentences.zh: 这种急剧衰退与这座城市自身的后工业化崩溃如出一辙。

sentences.en: To reverse the trend,
sentences.zh: 为了扭转这一趋势，

sentences.en: Ravitch prepared a detailed breakdown of the costs of repairing and replacing all of the system's outdated equipment and proposed a sweeping plan to help fund the work.
sentences.zh: 拉维奇详细列出了修复和更换该系统所有老化设备的成本明细，并提出了帮助筹集资金的全面计划。

sentences.en: He argued at the time, the transit situation, though lacking the drama of imminent bankruptcy, represents an equally grave threat to our economy, the social equilibrium,
sentences.zh: 他当时辩称，公交困境虽然没有迫在眉睫的破产那样具有戏剧性，但对我们的经济、社会平衡

sentences.en: and the survival of the greatest city in the world.
sentences.zh: 以及世界上最伟大城市的生存构成了同样严重的威胁。

sentences.en: The subway's importance to the city begins with a single, durable economic principle.
sentences.zh: 地铁对这座城市的重要性始于一个持久的经济原则。

sentences.en: Cities create density, and density creates growth.
sentences.zh: 城市创造密度，密度创造增长。

sentences.en: Economists call the phenomenon agglomeration.
sentences.zh: 经济学家将这种现象称为集聚。

sentences.en: Not only does geographical proximity reduce costs, but it also facilitates the exchange of knowledge and spurs innovation.
sentences.zh: 地理上的临近不仅降低了成本，还促进了知识交流并激发了创新。

sentences.en: It's a principle that holds true for better and worse, and regardless of the industry.
sentences.zh: 这一原则无论好坏、不分行业都同样适用。

sentences.en: The free market economist
sentences.zh: 自由市场经济学家

sentences.en: Edward Glazer has pointed out that the junk bonds and leveraged buyouts of 70s and 80s Wall Street were as much the product of human collaboration as they were of corporate greed.
sentences.zh: 爱德华·格莱泽指出，70和80年代华尔街的垃圾债券和杠杆收购，既是人类合作的产物，也是企业贪婪的结果。

sentences.en: The urban planning professor
sentences.zh: 城市规划教授

sentences.en: Elizabeth Currid-Halkett coined the phrase the Warhol economy to describe how this same sort of cross-fertilization and idea-sharing works in New York's art, fashion,
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白·柯里德-哈尔基特创造了“沃霍尔经济”一词，来描述这种同类交叉融合与创意分享如何在纽约的艺术、时尚

sentences.en: and music worlds.
sentences.zh: 和音乐界运作。

sentences.en: As industries grow, they attract and create new connected ones.
sentences.zh: 随着行业的发展，它们吸引并催生了新的相关行业。

sentences.en: Book publishers beget book agents, tech startups beget venture capital firms, and so on.
sentences.zh: 图书出版商催生了图书经纪人，科技初创公司催生了风险投资公司，诸如此类。

sentences.en: It all begins with the ability to pack large numbers of people
sentences.zh: 这一切都始于将大量人群塞进

sentences.en: spaces and then unpack them at the end of the day.
sentences.zh: 空间并在一天结束时将他们疏散的能力。

sentences.en: Without the subway, this process breaks down and the city dissipates.
sentences.zh: 如果没有地铁，这个过程就会崩溃，城市也会消散。

sentences.en: Ravitch took his case to editorial boards and legislative leaders, but there was a problem.
sentences.zh: 拉维奇带着他的方案找到了各大报社编辑部和立法领袖，但问题来了。

sentences.en: No one wanted new taxes.
sentences.zh: 没有人想要新税。

sentences.en: So Ravitch cold-called
sentences.zh: 于是拉维奇直接打电话给

sentences.en: David Rockefeller, the longtime head of Chase Manhattan Bank.
sentences.zh: 大通曼哈顿银行长期掌门人大卫·洛克菲勒。

sentences.en: I said,
sentences.zh: 我说，

sentences.en: Mr. Rockefeller, this is an audacious request, but would you get up at five in the morning and let me show you the subway system?
sentences.zh: 洛克菲勒先生，这是一个很大胆的请求，但你愿意早上五点起床让我带你参观一下地铁系统吗？

sentences.en: He told me one afternoon in his office at Waterside, and he said yes.
sentences.zh: 他在滨水区的办公室里向我讲述了这个下午，并说他答应了。

sentences.en: Ravitch then suggested that Rockefeller bring along the chairman of MetLife and the president of AT&T.
sentences.zh: 拉维奇随后建议洛克菲勒带上大都会人寿保险公司的董事长和美国电话电报公司的总裁。

sentences.en: All three went and saw the dirty, graffiti-scarred system firsthand.
sentences.zh: 这三个人都去实地参观了这个肮脏、布满涂鸦的系统。

sentences.en: As Ravitch tells the story, that was all it took.
sentences.zh: 正如拉维奇所说的那样，只需这么做就够了。

sentences.en: Rockefeller called the majority leader of the state Senate and told him to give Ravitch what he needs.
sentences.zh: 洛克菲勒打电话给州参议院多数党领袖，告诉他给拉维奇想要的一切。

sentences.en: The tax package passed and Ravitch ultimately raised
sentences.zh: 税收方案通过了，拉维奇最终筹集了

sentences.zh: 77亿美元，相当于如今的170多亿美元，其中大部分用于更换车辆、翻新车站和加强维护。

sentences.en: The turnaround was not immediate.
sentences.zh: 情况并没有立刻好转。

sentences.en: A year after
sentences.zh: 在

sentences.en: Ravitch's tax plan was enacted, annual subway ridership dropped below
sentences.zh: 拉维奇的税收计划实施一年后，年度地铁客流量降到了

sentences.en: $1 billion.
sentences.zh: 10亿人次以下。

sentences.en: But before long, as the system gradually became safer, more reliable, and less unsavory, it started to trend up.
sentences.zh: 但没过多久，随着系统逐渐变得更加安全、可靠且不再那么令人不快，客流量开始回升。

sentences.en: By 2015, ridership had hit
sentences.zh: 到2015年，客流量已达到

sentences.en: $1.7 billion, a level not seen since the late 1940s.
sentences.zh: 17亿人次，达到了自20世纪40年代末以来从未有过的水平。

sentences.en: The rejuvenation of the subway has been intertwined with a protracted period of staggering economic prosperity.
sentences.zh: 地铁的复苏与一段惊人的经济繁荣期交织在一起。

sentences.en: agglomeration at work.
sentences.zh: 这就是集聚效应在起作用。

sentences.en: New York rebuilt the subway and the subway rebuilt the city.
sentences.zh: 纽约重建了地铁，地铁重建了城市。

sentences.en: It was one of the great urban renaissance stories of our modern era.
sentences.zh: 这是我们现代最具传奇色彩的城市复兴故事之一。

sentences.en: But now that the city is thriving, it faces another challenge, perhaps an even greater one.
sentences.zh: 但现在，当这座城市欣欣向荣时，它面临着另一个挑战，也许是一个更大的挑战。

sentences.en: How to spread this staggering wealth more evenly.
sentences.zh: 如何更均匀地分配这笔惊人的财富。

sentences.en: The subway might again be a central part part of the solution.
sentences.zh: 地铁或许可以再次成为解决方案的核心部分。

sentences.en: If the story of the subway is the story of density, it is also the story of land.
sentences.zh: 如果说地铁的故事是关于密度的故事，那么它也是关于土地的故事。

sentences.en: And more to the point, the story of land value.
sentences.zh: 更确切地说，是关于土地价值的故事。

sentences.en: Before the first tracks had even been laid, real estate speculators were gobbling up farmland and empty lots along the proposed route, and then quickly flipping their parcels
sentences.zh: 甚至在铺设第一条轨道之前，房地产投机者就在拟建路线沿线抢购农田和空地，然后迅速将他们的地块

sentences.en: at huge premiums to builders.
sentences.zh: 以高昂的溢价转手给建筑商。

sentences.en: When the subway recovered from its last major crisis, it again began throwing off enormous returns for the owners of the land above it.
sentences.zh: 当地铁从上一场重大危机中恢复过来时，它又开始为其上方土地的所有者带来巨额回报。

sentences.en: From 1993 to 2013, the average price for a co-op or condo in Tribeca rose from $182 per square foot to $1,569.
sentences.zh: 从1993年到2013年，翠贝卡区合作公寓或共管公寓的平均价格从每平方英尺182美元涨到了1569美元。

sentences.en: In the process, prime real estate in Manhattan was transformed from a place where people lived and built businesses into a high-yield investment in which absentee owners
sentences.zh: 在此过程中，曼哈顿的黄金地段从人们居住和建立企业的地方，变成了缺席业主

sentences.en: parked their money and watched it grow.
sentences.zh: 存入资金并看着它不断增值的高收益投资。

sentences.en: As Manhattan's business district centers became denser and its scarce real estate more expensive, the growth started to spill out, following the subway's snaking lines
sentences.zh: 随着曼哈顿商业区中心变得更加密集、稀缺的房地产价格更加昂贵，这种增长开始溢出，沿着地铁蜿蜒的线路

sentences.en: across the river into Brooklyn and Queens.
sentences.zh: 跨过河流进入布鲁克林和皇后区。

sentences.en: Developers build things where the subway works, and we build far fewer things where it doesn't.
sentences.zh: 开发商在地铁通达的地方建房，而在地铁不通的地方我们建得要少得多。

sentences.en: Jed Walentis, the 43-year-old principal of the real estate development company
sentences.zh: 杰德·瓦伦蒂斯，这位43岁房地产开发公司

sentences.en: Two Trees Management told me recently over lunch at a cafe in Dumbo,
sentences.zh: “双树管理”的负责人最近在布鲁克林丹波区一家咖啡馆吃午饭时告诉我，

sentences.en: Brooklyn's answer to Soho.
sentences.zh: 丹波就是布鲁克林的苏荷区。

sentences.en: We put density where there's transit.
sentences.zh: 我们在有交通的地方注入密度。

sentences.en: Walentis, who was wearing the familiar Brooklyn uniform of jeans,
sentences.zh: 瓦伦蒂斯穿着布鲁克林的标志性装扮——牛仔裤、

sentences.en: New Balance sneakers, and a blue hoodie, and his father,
sentences.zh: 新百伦运动鞋和一件蓝色连帽衫，他和他的父亲

sentences.en: David, own a good chunk of Dumbo, an investment that has made them rich, house in the Hamptons, vacations, heliskiing, beyond the wildest dreams of most New Yorkers.
sentences.zh: 大卫拥有丹波的大片土地，这项投资让他们变得富有，拥有汉普顿的别墅、度假、直升机滑雪，超越了大多数纽约人最疯狂的梦想。

sentences.en: I've known Walentis since the early 2000s when I rented a desk in one of his many buildings in the neighborhood, a turn-of-the-century factory that has since been converted
sentences.zh: 我和瓦伦蒂斯从21世纪初就认识了，当时我在他该社区的众多大楼里租了一个办公桌，那是一座建于世纪之交的工厂，后来被改建成

sentences.en: into multi-million-dollar condominiuMs.
sentences.zh: 了价值数百万美元的公寓。

sentences.en: This is pretty representative of Dumbo's overall trajectory over the last two decades.
sentences.zh: 这很能代表丹波过去二十年的整体发展轨迹。

sentences.en: It's a stark transformation that would have been impossible to predict when his father first started buying up the neighborhood's underutilized properties in the early 1980s
sentences.zh: 这是一个鲜明的转变，当他的父亲在20世纪80年代初开始收购该社区未充分利用的房产时，这是根本无法预料的，

sentences.en: before it was widely known as Dumbo.
sentences.zh: 当时这里还远不如丹波那样闻名遐迩。

sentences.en: What enabled it to happen wasn't just the neighborhood's excellent subway access, it's sandwiched between the F-Line and the A-Line, or the city's economic recovery,
sentences.zh: 促成这一切的不仅仅是该社区极佳的地铁交通（它夹在F线和A线之间），或者是城市的经济复苏，

sentences.en: or even the exodus of rich people priced out of Manhattan by even richer people.
sentences.zh: 甚至也不是因为被更富有的人挤出曼哈顿的富人大量外流。

sentences.en: The transformation of Dumbo required something much simpler, a change in the zoning law.
sentences.zh: 丹波的转变需要更简单得多的东西——分区法的改变。

sentences.en: For years, the neighborhood had been restricted to only manufacturing uses, a legacy of the city's losing battle to retain industrial jobs in the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 多年来，该社区一直仅限于制造业用途，这是该市在20世纪60年代为保留工业就业岗位而进行的一场失利之战的遗留产物。

sentences.en: In the late 90s,
sentences.zh: 在90年代末，

sentences.zh: 瓦伦蒂斯和他的父亲成功说服市政府抛弃这些旧规定，允许他们彻底改造该社区，将老旧工厂填满阁楼公寓、

sentences.zh: 设计和科技中心办公室、零售店、艺术家工作室和新的公寓大楼。

sentences.en: In the subsequent 20 years, as the neighborhood changed, average condo prices rose from $200 per square foot to more than $1,500.
sentences.zh: 在随后的20年里，随着社区的变迁，公寓平均价格从每平方英尺200美元涨到了1500多美元。

sentences.en: More recently,
sentences.zh: 最近，

sentences.zh: 瓦伦蒂斯向北推进到威廉斯堡，利用那里的类似重新分区，将L地铁线附近的前纺织厂变成时尚的怀斯酒店，并将19世纪的

sentences.en: domino sugar refinery,
sentences.zh: 多米诺糖厂，

sentences.zh: 即J、M和Z线沿线，改造成了300万平方英尺的办公空间、零售店、公园和公寓。

sentences.en: Like most good government tools, zoning sounds boring, but it is, in fact, a secret means by which cities are shaped and fortunes are made.
sentences.zh: 就像大多数优秀的政府工具一样，分区听起来很无聊，但事实上，它是塑造城市和创造财富的秘密手段。

sentences.en: If the subway delivers density, zoning determines where that density goes by doing things like placing limits on how tall buildings can rise or how many dwellings they can contain.
sentences.zh: 如果说地铁带来了密度，那么分区则通过对建筑物的高度或包含的住宅数量设定限制等手段，决定了这种密度流向何方。

sentences.en: New York's zoning codes are Byzantine, the product of years of pushing and pulling between the desire to allow the city to evolve and grow and the impulse
sentences.zh: 纽约的分区法典极其繁复，是多年来各方博弈的产物，一方希望允许城市演进和生长，另一方则冲动地

sentences.en: to keep development in check.
sentences.zh: 想要遏制开发。

sentences.en: These codes have helped preserve the city's historic buildings and neighborhoods while preventing its streets from being forever cast into darkness by endless rows of skyscrapers.
sentences.zh: 这些法典有助于保护城市的历史建筑和社区，同时防止街道被一排排无尽的摩天大楼永远笼罩在黑暗之中。

sentences.en: But they have also had the effect of restricting the supply of housing, which has driven up prices, especially in neighborhoods with desirable buildings and good subway access.
sentences.zh: 但它们也起到了限制住房供应的作用，从而推高了价格，尤其是那些拥有令人向往的建筑和良好地铁交通的社区。

sentences.zh: 我以每月3400美元的价格出租单身公寓，

sentences.en: It doesn't make any sense.
